summary: Galaxy Health is evaluating Redwood for PII-bearing clinical NLP workflows. CISO and Lead DevOps focused on SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration, and data residency. They are primarily interested in Dedicated or Private deployments but want Hosted security controls and attestation before committing to a pilot. Next steps: send compliance docs, schedule benchmark for dedicated pool, and follow up on network requirements.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-11
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Park (CISO, Galaxy), Marcus Li (Lead DevOps), Sasha Nguyen (PM)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, yeah really appreciate it. this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. with me are Priya and Luis from our security and infra team.
[00:06] Dr. Elena Park: Thanks. we've been looking at a few providers, want to get granular on security posture before we talk pilots. we handle PHI so SOC2 and iso are must-haves.
[00:14] Priya: absolutely, we understand. quick high-level first: Redwood offers Hosted, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). for regulated workloads a lot of customers go Dedicated or Private but we also have controls for Hosted like data isolation, retention flags, and encryption.
[00:30] Marcus: can you point me to the attestation reports? we'll need SOC2 type II and ISO 27001.
[00:36] Jordan: yes i'll share the PDFs after the call, plus a compliance questionnaire.
[00:40] Luis: just to add — our SOC2 covers the inference platform, ops, and network controls. ISO covers our information security management. we'll send the latest certs, and there's also a summary doc that highlights scoping and any carve-outs.
[00:52] Dr. Elena Park: great. on authentication — we use enterprise SSO via SAML with SCIM for provisioning. do you support SSO/SAML and SCIM?
[01:00] Priya: yes, SAML 2.0, IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. SCIM for user sync is available for RBAC. For Dedicated and Private we can integrate with customer-managed IdP inside the VPC; for Hosted we offer SAML + SCIM and single-tenant provisioning options.
[01:18] Marcus: and RBAC — we need fine-grained roles, ability to restrict access to models and endpoints, and auditability.
[01:24] Priya: we have role-based access controls with pre-defined roles and custom role support. you can scope roles to projects, models, and routes. all actions are logged — admin API calls, model deployments, keys.
[01:36] Sasha: what's the fidelity of logs? retention windows? we have retention policies for 7 years for some records.
[01:42] Luis: default audit logs retention on Hosted is 90 days, but for Dedicated and Private we support longer retention windows and can ship logs to your SIEM. for enterprise contracts we do custom retention and on-prem archive integrations.
[01:58] Dr. Elena Park: shipping logs to our SIEM — is that push or pull? what formats?
[02:04] Priya: we can push via secure syslog, or you can pull from our log export API. formats are structured JSON and CSV exports; we also offer direct Cloud Pub/Sub or Kinesis connectors depending on region. we'll include a doc with exact endpoints and TLS requirements.
[02:20] Marcus: encryption at rest and in transit — of course. KMS? HSM? where are customer keys stored?
[02:26] Luis: TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit. at rest all model artifacts and logs are encrypted. we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). for Private deployments you can bring your own HSM. For Hosted we offer CMKs where customers retain control in the cloud provider's KMS.
[02:44] Dr. Elena Park: any multi-tenancy concerns — we can't have PHI commingled with other tenants.
[02:50] Jordan: understood. for Dedicated you're running in an isolated GPU pool. Private gives you complete network isolation and a private control plane option. for Hosted we have strict logical isolation and contract-level commitments; many customers with PHI choose Dedicated or Private to avoid multi-tenant risk.
[03:06] Sasha: what's the process for key rotation and access revocation?
[03:10] Priya: keys can be rotated via your KMS policies; we support rolling rotations and immediate revocation. our audit logs capture KMS access and key operations. for Dedicated we can assist with operational runbooks.
[03:22] Marcus: okay, on data flows — can you confirm whether any data is used for model training or telemetry? we need no training on customer data.
[03:30] Luis: Redwood does not use customer inference data to train models by default. we have an opt-in program for aggregated telemetry improvements but for enterprise PHI customers it's disabled by contract. we'll put that in writing in the DPA and contract.
[03:44] Dr. Elena Park: good. what's your data residency footprint — can we pin data to us-east or an on-prem footprint?
[03:50] Jordan: yes, Dedicated customers can choose region and we support private on-prem for full data residency. Hosted can be region-restricted for data at rest but not fully on-prem. we'll provide region map and available regions for Dedicated.
[04:04] Sasha: latency vs cost — if we go Dedicated what kind of latency numbers can we expect for short clinical note generation (<=256 tokens)?
[04:12] Priya: typical p95 latency on Dedicated for 256 tokens is in the 120-200ms range, depends on model size and quantization. Hosted may have slightly higher variance. we'll propose a benchmark run.
[04:26] Marcus: and throughput — we have 200 qps peak. can dedicated GPU pools handle that?
[04:32] Luis: yes, with autoscaling and GPU pooling you can provision predictable throughput. we can size a Dedicated pool to meet 200 qps with target latency SLOs; pricing depends on reserved capacity. we'll scope in the POC.
[04:46] Dr. Elena Park: audit trails — we need exportable trails for compliance audits. can you provide immutable logs and time-stamped events?
[04:54] Priya: yes, we provide append-only audit logs with timestamps, user IDs, and event types. for Private/Dedicated you can ship to your SIEM and retain per your policy. we also support signed log export bundles for audits.
[05:06] Sasha: any third-party pen tests or vulnerability scanning schedules?
[05:10] Luis: we run quarterly vulnerability scans and annual third-party pen tests; results are summarized in redacted form in our compliance pack. we also have a bug bounty program.
[05:20] Dr. Elena Park: where do you stand with FedRAMP or HITRUST?
[05:24] Jordan: we don't have FedRAMP yet; HITRUST is on the roadmap but not certified. we do have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001. for many healthcare customers we do private deployments or contractual safeguards while we pursue additional certifications.
[05:38] Marcus: network ingress/egress — we need explicit IP allow lists and egress controls.
[05:42] Priya: Dedicated and Private support IP allow lists, private peering, and VPC endpoints. Hosted has IP allow lists and per-project network controls. we'll send sample firewall rules and peering configs.
[05:56] Dr. Elena Park: incident response — do you have runbooks and SLAs for security incidents?
[06:00] Luis: yes, we maintain incident response plans, notify customers within defined windows for severity levels, and provide post-incident reports. SLA details are in the enterprise contract addendum.
[06:10] Sasha: curious about RBAC for model access specifically — can we prevent some teams from deploying new models to production?
[06:16] Priya: yes, deploy permissions are separate from invoke permissions. you can create a deployment-only or invoke-only roles.
[06:22] Jordan: just to reiterate, many of these controls are available across modes but the higher isolation and customizability come with Dedicated and Private.
[06:30] Marcus: what about secrets management for API keys and model secrets?
[06:34] Luis: API keys are scoped and can be rotated; for Dedicated we can integrate with your secret manager so keys never leave your network. for Hosted we store keys encrypted and can integrate with customer KMS for CMKs.
[06:48] Dr. Elena Park: ok timeline — we're hoping to start a pilot in 4-6 weeks if compliance checks are clean.
[06:54] Jordan: that timeline is doable. next steps I'll send SOC2/ISO certs and the compliance questionnaire; Priya will attach architecture and dedicated sizing notes; and Marcus will share network diagrams.
[07:06] Sasha: can we also get a sample contract clause about no-training-on-customer-data?
[07:10] Jordan: yes we'll include that sample DPA clause.
[07:14] Luis: any specific security tooling you require for the POC?
[07:18] Marcus: we'll want SIEM ingestion and endpoint allow lists. also, we may do a short pen test against the dedicated endpoint as part of the POC.
[07:26] Priya: that's fine; we'll coordinate with our infra team and set scope.
[07:30] Dr. Elena Park: one last question — what's your approach to data deletion and retention if we terminate?
[07:36] Luis: we support certified data deletion workflows; we can provide a deletion certificate and support escrow backups and lifecycle policies. for Hosted we have retention flags and deletion APIs; for Private you control the data lifecycle entirely.
[07:50] Jordan: thanks everyone. recap of action items and deliverables — I'll follow up with docs and schedule the benchmark to validate latency and throughput.
[07:58] Sasha: thanks, appreciate it.

[end of recording]
